hypothesis_change_reason: Materially different diagnosis with a different remedy set. The previous hypothesis claimed the released runtime v1.0.0 is defective and that the fix is to adopt the core's uncommitted working tree and re-materialize the project. This dispatch ran the single-variable control the previous dispatch never ran and falsified that: the project's own released runtime passes 36/36 (exit 0) when it is paired with its own released core root, and fails the identical 7 behaviours when the same project bytes are paired with the uncommitted core root. The causal variable is the PAIRING of project materialized bytes with the core root's working-tree revision, not the runtime version and not the project tree.

narrative.FINDING: W57's non-acceptance red (validate-managed-runtime.py exit 1 with 7 behaviour failures) is caused by the project being paired with a core root whose working tree is an uncommitted revision, not by any defect in the project's released runtime, and not by anything in W57's owned scope.
narrative.OBSERVED_FAILURE: validate-managed-runtime.py exit 1, 29 PASS / 7 FAIL. Failing behaviours: controller_semantic_counters_vs_retries, progress_contract_v1_v2_deterministic, audit_close_todo_semantic_history, controller_worker_timeout_serial_parallel_barrier, multi_group_managed_parallel_synthetic_base, parallel_cross_wave_true_owner_routing, v2_plan_gate_before_run_repair. All 7 abort early (6.7s-42.1s) with 'unexpected dispatch plan; next scripted=[...]' or 'multi-group run did not complete', i.e. the controller never reaches the scripted dispatch.
narrative.HYPOTHESIS: The 7 failures are produced by a mixed-revision pairing: the project's managed files are released core v1.0.0 bytes while AC_CORE_ROOT resolves to the canonical core's uncommitted working tree. Under a consistent pairing (v1.0.0 project + v1.0.0 core root, or WIP project + WIP core root) the same suite is green.
narrative.CHANGE: Built two new scratch arms under .tmp/w57-repair-126/ that hold the tree, the managed-file bytes and the temp root constant and vary only the core root: a pristine released core root extracted with 'git archive v1.0.0' (zero WIP) versus the live D:\Projeler\.agents-core working tree. No project or core file was edited; no lock was released; no re-materialization was run.
narrative.RESULT: Hypothesis confirmed. The project's released runtime is fully green (36/36, exit 0) against a released core root and reproduces the identical 7 FAILs (exit 1) against the uncommitted core root. Two prior-dispatch claims are falsified and the remedy set changes.

B_stub_tree_wip_bytes_wip_core_root.note: Reproduced here only as a prior observation; not re-run. Its test inventory is a strict superset (5-7 extra behaviours added by the WIP harness), which is why a raw pass-count comparison across A and B is not a valid contrast. This dispatch's arms C and E avoid that confound because both run the same v1.0.0 harness.

C_released_bytes_released_core_root.core_root: pristine 'git archive v1.0.0' extraction, zero uncommitted bytes

controlled_comparison.single_variable: AC_CORE_ROOT only (released v1.0.0 archive vs uncommitted working tree). Tree contents, all 110 managed-file sha256 values, the validator binary itself, the working directory shape and TEMP/TMP were held identical between arm C and arm E and verified equal by sha256 before the runs.
controlled_comparison.result: C exit 0 (36/36 PASS) vs E exit 1 (29 PASS / 7 FAIL, the same 7 behaviours with byte-identical error strings as arm A).
controlled_comparison.conclusion: The core root's revision state is sufficient and necessary to reproduce the red. The project's released runtime is not defective. The real repository's tree state is not a contributing factor (arm C and arm E share a stub tree and differ only in core root).

causal_model.statement: The project is materialized at released core v1.0.0 (byte-exact; proven in dispatch 124 and re-confirmed here: the working-tree CRLF sha256 of run-wave-program.py, 2427267d..., equals the LF-normalized sha256 of the v1.0.0 blob, and the stub arms reproduce the project bytes exactly). AC_CORE_ROOT resolves to the canonical core, whose working tree is an uncommitted WIP on top of HEAD=73c1b7d8=tag v1.0.0. Whenever the runtime executes with that mixed pairing it fails closed before reaching the scripted dispatch, producing the 7 early-abort behaviour failures. Whenever the pairing is self-consistent it is green.
four_arm_consistency: project v1.0.0 + core WIP   -> FAIL 7 (arm A, arm E)
project v1.0.0 + core v1.0.0 -> PASS 36/36 (arm C)
project WIP   + core WIP     -> PASS 41/41 (arm B, prior dispatch)
causal_model.timing_signature: In arm C the same behaviours run to completion (controller_semantic_counters_vs_retries 27.2s, progress_contract_v1_v2_deterministic 88.5s, audit_close_todo_semantic_history 102.5s, multi_group_managed_parallel_synthetic_base 87.7s, parallel_cross_wave_true_owner_routing 96.8s); in arm E they abort at 6.7s-11.5s. The failures are a pre-dispatch abort, not a behavioural regression.

prior_phase_claims_falsified.prior_claim: W57_REPAIR124/125 remedy step 2: 'commit or discard the dirty core paths, then run materialize-ac-core.py to re-materialize the project', presented as required.
prior_phase_claims_falsified.falsification: Re-materialization of the project is not required to clear the 7 behaviour failures. The project is already at the released bytes; only the core root disagrees. Arm C proves a fully green world with the project's existing released bytes. A re-materialization would additionally import 2188 insertions of uncommitted, unreleased core WIP (diffstat measured this dispatch) and would require a controller restart over controller_restart_paths. It is one of two remedy branches, not a prerequisite.

discarded_probe.probe: python .opencode\scripts\materialization_guard.py --check (run in the real repo and in both stub trees, with AC_CORE_ROOT set in the environment)
discarded_probe.why_discarded: materialization_guard.py's main() resolves its core from --core only; it never reads AC_CORE_ROOT. Without --core, check_materialization(repo, None) skips every core-root-dependent check, so the probe could not observe the core root at all. Its 'PASS' in the real repo and 'STALE' in the stubs reflect only per-file sha256 comparison against the stub's own older manifest and LF-vs-CRLF byte differences, not any finding about the core root. No conclusion in this artifact rests on it.
discarded_probe.mutation_check: The probe is read-only (--write is the only mutating mode). The tracked manifest .opencode/protocol/AC_CORE_MATERIALIZATION.json is unmodified (git status clean for that path), core_revision still 50549a1abbc44e49, materialized_at still 2026-09-27T18:01:03, mtime unchanged at 2026-09-27 21:14:59.

not_required_anymore: Project-side re-materialization as a precondition for the 7 behaviour failures (only R2 needs it).
Any change to .opencode/scripts/*, .agents/* or any other managed file in this repository.
Any W57 product, test, evidence or lifecycle change. The W57-owned defect ledger, freeze declaration, support matrix and candidate content are untouched by this finding.

why_W57_cannot_clear_it: The inconsistent artifact is the core's own working tree, in a different repository. W57 has no authority over it, and AGENTS.md forbids a second substantive Wave policy tree outside .agents/.

Committing or discarding 40 uncommitted paths in another repository is a release/destructive act requiring explicit current-conversation approval, which this dispatch does not have. Discarding would destroy the owner's WIP; committing would publish unreleased policy.

The project's sanctioned re-materialization tool refuses while the live controller holds the lock (dispatch 124 recorded EXIT=3, 'live controller: ac-wave-opencode-parallel.lock pid=51592'), and releasing the controller's own lock from inside its own dispatch would weaken a safety invariant.

W57's machine-owned scope is FREEZE-*/TODO-*/PKGREG-*; global_bookkeeping_owner is controller. Canonical-core revision control is neither. A fourth REOPEN cycle on this finding has no remaining W57-side lever, which this dispatch proved by single-variable isolation rather than by assertion.
